statements.t: We intend to continue to implement our business strategy, reinforce customer loyalty and remain a market leader by continuing to develop our Rush Truck Centers as we expand our product offerings and extend our dealership network through strategic acquisitions of new locations and opening new locations in our existing areas of operation to enable us to better serve our customers.
We also intend to continue to grow by acquiring or investing in businesses that are adjacent to our commercial vehicle dealership business.
We expect that new Class 8 truck orders will normalize once customers have more information from both the EPA and manufacturers.
We expect our U.S. market share of new Class 8 truck sales to range between 6.3% and 6.5% in 2026 based on A.C.T.
We expect to sell approximately 450 new Class 8 trucks in Canada in 2026.
We believe that demand for new medium-duty vehicles will remain stable for the remainder of the year, although production delays may impact the timing of deliveries.
We expect our U.S. market share of new Class 4 through 7 commercial vehicle sales to range between 5.3% and 5.5% in 2026 based on A.C.T.
We expect to sell approximately 1,000 new Class 5 through 7 commercial vehicles in Canada in 2026.

We expect to sell approximately 3,500 light-duty vehicles and approximately 7,000 used commercial vehicles in 2026, and we expect lease and rental revenue to increase approximately 3.2% during 2026, compared to 2025.

With respect to our parts, service, and collision center (collectively referred to herein as “Aftermarket Products and Services”) operations, while the aftermarket recovery continues to trail the improvements in new commercial vehicle sales, we expect aftermarket demand to gradually improve through the end of the year, subject to normal seasonal patterns.
We expect blended gross margins on Aftermarket Products and Services operations to range from 35.5% to 37.5% in 2026.
For 2026, we expect overall gross margins from new Class 8 truck sales of approximately 7.5% to 8.0%.

For 2026, we expect overall gross margins from new medium-duty commercial vehicle sales of approximately 7.5% to 8.0%, but this will largely depend upon the mix of purchasers and types of vehicles sold.
We expect margins on used commercial vehicles to range between 12.0% and 15.0% in 2026.
We expect gross margins from lease and rental sales of approximately 28.0% to 30.0% during 2026.
For 2026, we expect SG&A expenses as a percentage of total revenues to range from 13.0% to 14.0%.
For 2026, we expect the selling portion of SG&A expenses to be approximately 25.0% to 30.0% of new and used commercial vehicle gross profit.

We expect net interest expense in 2026 to decrease compared to 2025, but the amount of the change will depend on inventory levels, interest rate fluctuations and the amount of cash available to make prepayments on our floor plan arrangements.
We expect our effective tax rate to be approximately 22.0% to 23.0% of pretax income in 2026.

We believe we will have sufficient liquidity to meet our debt service and working capital requirements, commitments and contingencies, debt repayments, acquisitions, capital expenditures and any operating requirements for at least the next twelve months.
We do not anticipate any breach of these covenants in the foreseeable future.
We expect to purchase or lease commercial vehicles worth approximately $300.0 million to $325.0 million for our leasing operations during 2026, depending on customer demand.

We also expect to make capital expenditures for the purchase of recurring items such as computers, shop tools and equipment and company vehicles of approximately $35.0 million to $40.0 million during 2026.
We expect to continue paying cash dividends on a quarterly basis.

However, there is no assurance as to future dividends because the declaration and payment of such dividends is subject to the business judgment of our Board of Directors and will depend on historic and projected earnings, capital requirements, covenant compliance and financial conditions and such other factors as our Board of Directors deem relevant.

The actual timing, number of shares and value of repurchases under the stock repurchase program will be determined by management at its discretion and will depend on a number of factors, including market conditions, stock price and other factors.
We anticipate funding the capital expenditures for the improvement and expansion of existing facilities and recurring expenses through our operating cash flows.
Orders from several of our major fleet customers are included in our backlog as of September 30, 2026, and we expect to fill the majority of our backlog orders by the end of 2026.
We have incurred, and will continue to incur, capital and operating expenditures and other costs in complying with such laws and regulations.
In addition, in connection with acquisitions, it is possible that we will assume or become subject to new or unforeseen environmental costs or liabilities, some of which may be material.
One of the EPA’s engine emissions rules that we believe will become effective is referred to herein as the “EPA 2027 Low NOx” rule.

With respect to the legal challenges to the EPA’s repeal of the Endangerment Finding, we do not expect that any successful challenge will result in the prior GHG rules and regulations becoming effective in the near term.

statements.t: We believe that our results reflect the continued improvement of freight markets following the extended industry downcycle, and we expect that improvement to continue in the fourth quarter,” Rush said.

We believe that the successful execution of these initiatives will allow us to better serve our customers’ needs, which we believe will position us to deliver greater value to both customers and shareholders over the long term,” he continued.
“Looking ahead, we expect aftermarket demand to continue to gradually improve through the remainder of the year, subject to normal seasonal patterns.
We believe these efforts will help us capture additional aftermarket business and meet more of our customers’ ongoing maintenance and repair needs,” he added.

“Our current backlog suggests that our new commercial vehicle sales will be strong in the fourth quarter and into the first quarter of 2027, although supply capacity constraints may affect the timing of deliveries.

On a positive note, while the timing of future orders for commercial vehicles remains uncertain, we believe that industry demand for new Class 8 trucks is still healthy and that orders will pick up shortly after the EPA finalizes its rules.
We believe our strategy will provide us with a competitive advantage and allow us to serve customers who need medium-duty equipment in the near term,” he continued.
Additionally, we experienced less seasonal slowdown than we typically see in used truck demand, and we expect demand to remain strong through the fourth quarter and into early 2027.
“We expect rental demand to remain strong through the fourth quarter and into early 2027, as customers evaluate alternatives to purchasing higher-priced commercial vehicles.
However, we believe that leasing demand may soften in the first quarter of 2027 due to the fact that many customers purchased replacement vehicles ahead of anticipated new 2027 model price increases.

We believe that our approach will help customers manage their fleets in the most efficient manner and keep their vehicles up and running, while also providing us with more opportunities to strengthen those relationships and earn more of each customer’s business in areas where we may not be as strong today.
